learn.hook: Out of sixteen great janapadas, one grew into the heart of India's first big empire. What made Magadha so special?
points: Magadha lay in the fertile middle Ganga plains, in present-day Bihar. Its farms grew plenty of rice and other crops.
It had rich iron-ore deposits nearby (in present-day Jharkhand), so it could make strong tools and weapons.
Its forests supplied elephants for the army and timber for building. Rivers like the Ganga and Son helped transport and trade.
Its early capital Rājagṛiha was protected by hills; the later capital Pāṭaliputra (today's Patna) stood on the Ganga.
Strong rulers expanded it: Bimbisāra and Ajātashatru (Haryanka dynasty), then the Shishunāgas and the very wealthy Nandas.

example.q: List two ways in which geography helped Magadha become powerful.
steps: Fertile land gave surplus food and taxes.
Nearby iron ore gave tools and weapons.
Forests gave elephants for the army; rivers helped trade and the movement of soldiers.
example.answer: Any two: fertile land, iron ore, forests with elephants, and rivers for transport.

learn.reallife: When you visit Rajgir or Patna in Bihar, you are walking where Magadha's capitals stood more than 2,000 years ago.

quiz.q: Magadha was located mainly in present-day:
quiz.explain: Magadha lay in the middle Ganga plains, in today's Bihar.
steps: Magadha lay in the fertile middle Ganga plains.
That area is present-day Bihar.
Gujarat, Kerala and Punjab are far from the middle Ganga plains.
Answer: Bihar
quiz.mistake: Does not place Magadha on the map

quiz.q: Which natural resource near Magadha helped it make strong weapons?
quiz.explain: Iron ore deposits allowed Magadha to make tools and weapons.
steps: Strong weapons were made of iron.
Magadha had rich iron-ore deposits nearby (in present-day Jharkhand).
So the resource is iron ore.
Answer: Iron ore
quiz.mistake: Does not link iron with weapons

quiz.q: Why were Magadha's forests important for its army?
quiz.explain: Elephants from the forests were a powerful part of Magadha's army.
steps: Magadha's forests supplied timber and animals.
Elephants from them were a powerful part of the army.
So the forests supplied elephants.
Answer: They supplied elephants
quiz.mistake: Thinks forests had no military use

quiz.q: What was Magadha's early capital, surrounded by hills?
quiz.explain: Rājagṛiha (Rajgir) was surrounded by hills, which gave natural protection.
steps: Magadha had an early and a later capital.
The early capital, Rājagṛiha (Rajgir), was protected by hills.
Pāṭaliputra was the later capital on the Ganga.
Answer: Rājagṛiha
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the early and later capitals

quiz.q: Pāṭaliputra, Magadha's later capital, is the modern city of:
quiz.explain: Pāṭaliputra grew on the Ganga at the site of present-day Patna.
steps: Pāṭaliputra stood on the Ganga.
It grew at the site of present-day Patna.
So the modern city is Patna.
Answer: Patna
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with another city on the Ganga

quiz.q: Which dynasty ruled Magadha just before the Mauryas?
quiz.explain: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the last Nanda king.
steps: Magadha's rulers: Haryankas, then Shishunāgas, then the Nandas.
Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the last Nanda king.
So the Nandas ruled just before the Mauryas.
Answer: The Nandas
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of dynasties

quiz.q: Bimbisāra and Ajātashatru belonged to which dynasty?
quiz.explain: They were early Haryanka rulers who expanded Magadha.
steps: Bimbisāra and Ajātashatru were early rulers who expanded Magadha.
They belonged to the Haryanka dynasty.
The Nandas and Mauryas came later.
Answer: Haryanka
quiz.mistake: Places them in a later dynasty

quiz.q: How did fertile land make Magadha stronger?
options: It meant no one had to work
More crops meant more food and more taxes for the ruler
quiz.explain: Surplus crops fed the people and the army, and taxes on them filled the treasury.
steps: Fertile land grew plenty of crops.
More crops meant food for the people and army, and taxes for the ruler.
So fertile land gave more food and more taxes.
Answer: More crops meant more food and more taxes for the ruler
quiz.mistake: Does not link agriculture with state power

teach.ask: Gappu asks why Magadha, of all places, became so powerful. Help him understand.
teach.praise: Fertile land, iron, elephants and rivers, plus strong rulers. Magadha had everything!
teach.nudge: Good! But what did Magadha use to make weapons, and where did its elephants come from?

revise.summary: Magadha, in present-day Bihar, grew powerful thanks to fertile land, nearby iron ore, forests with elephants and rivers for transport. Strong rulers from the Haryankas to the Nandas expanded it, with capitals at Rājagṛiha and later Pāṭaliputra.
focus: Know the order of dynasties before the Mauryas
Link fertile land with food, taxes and power
remember: Fertile Ganga plains (Bihar), iron ore (Jharkhand), forest elephants, the Ganga and Son rivers
Early capital Rājagṛiha (protected by hills); later Pāṭaliputra (Patna)
traps: Rājagṛiha was the early capital, not Pāṭaliputra
Bimbisāra and Ajātashatru were Haryankas, not Mauryas
The Nandas, not the Guptas, ruled just before the Mauryas

learn.hook: A young man and his wise teacher together built one of the largest empires India had ever seen.
points: Around 321 BCE, Chandragupta Maurya, guided by his teacher Chāṇakya (also called Kauṭilya), overthrew the Nandas and founded the Mauryan Empire, with Pāṭaliputra as its capital.
The Arthashāstra, linked with Kauṭilya, is a book on statecraft: how to run a kingdom, collect taxes, keep spies, manage trade and protect people.
The Arthashāstra describes seven 'limbs' (saptāṅga) of a state: the king, ministers, territory with its people, fort, treasury, army and allies.
Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus, lived at Chandragupta's court and wrote a book called Indica, which survives only in quotes by later writers.
Chandragupta's son Bindusāra and grandson Ashoka ruled after him. At its peak, the empire covered most of the subcontinent.

example.q: The Arthashāstra lists the treasury as one 'limb' of the state. Why would a kingdom be weak without it?
steps: A treasury stores the wealth collected from taxes.
This money pays soldiers, officials and builders of roads and forts.
Without it, the army and government could not work.
example.answer: Because without money the king cannot pay the army and officials who protect and run the kingdom.

learn.reallife: Chanakyapuri, a well-known area of New Delhi where many embassies are located, is named after Chāṇakya.

games.title: Mauryan names
pairs: Teacher and adviser linked with the Arthashāstra

quiz.q: Who founded the Mauryan Empire?
quiz.explain: Chandragupta Maurya founded it around 321 BCE.
steps: Around 321 BCE, the Nandas were overthrown and a new empire was founded.
Its founder was Chandragupta Maurya.
Ashoka was his grandson, not the founder.
Answer: Chandragupta Maurya
quiz.mistake: Confuses the founder with the most famous Mauryan, Ashoka

quiz.q: Who was Chandragupta's teacher and adviser?
quiz.explain: Chāṇakya, also known as Kauṭilya, guided Chandragupta.
steps: Chandragupta was guided by his teacher Chāṇakya.
Chāṇakya is also called Kauṭilya.
Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador, not his teacher.
Answer: Chāṇakya
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous people of different ages

quiz.q: The Arthashāstra is a book about:
quiz.explain: It discusses statecraft: government, taxes, army, trade and law.
steps: The Arthashāstra is a book on statecraft.
It explains running a kingdom: taxes, spies, trade and protecting people.
So it is about how to govern a state.
Answer: How to govern a state
quiz.mistake: Guesses the subject from the name alone

quiz.q: How many 'limbs' of the state does the saptāṅga idea describe?
quiz.explain: 'Sapta' means seven: king, ministers, territory with people, fort, treasury, army and allies.
steps: 'Sapta' means seven.
The limbs are king, ministers, territory with people, fort, treasury, army and allies.
Count them: 7.
Answer: 7
quiz.mistake: Does not know 'sapta' means seven

quiz.q: Megasthenes was:
options: A Greek ambassador at Chandragupta's court
A Buddhist monk from Sri Lanka
quiz.explain: Seleucus sent him to Pāṭaliputra, and he wrote Indica.
steps: Seleucus sent Megasthenes to Chandragupta's court.
He was a Greek ambassador who wrote Indica.
He was not a king, a Chinese traveller or a monk.
Answer: A Greek ambassador at Chandragupta's court
quiz.mistake: Confuses him with later Chinese travellers

quiz.q: What was the capital of the Mauryan Empire?
quiz.explain: Pāṭaliputra (Patna) was the Mauryan capital.
steps: Chandragupta founded the empire with its capital at Pāṭaliputra.
Pāṭaliputra is today's Patna.
So the capital was Pāṭaliputra.
Answer: Pāṭaliputra
quiz.mistake: Picks another important ancient city

quiz.q: Which is the correct order of Mauryan rulers?
quiz.explain: Chandragupta was followed by his son Bindusāra and then his grandson Ashoka.
steps: Chandragupta founded the empire.
His son Bindusāra ruled next, then his grandson Ashoka.
Order: Chandragupta, Bindusāra, Ashoka.
Answer: Chandragupta, Bindusāra, Ashoka
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of father, son and grandson

quiz.q: Why is the Arthashāstra's list of 'allies' important for a kingdom?
options: Friendly kingdoms can help in times of war and trade
quiz.explain: Good relations with other states make a kingdom safer and stronger.
steps: Allies are friendly kingdoms.
They can help in war and in trade.
This makes a kingdom safer and stronger.
Answer: Friendly kingdoms can help in times of war and trade
quiz.mistake: Does not understand what an ally is

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know how the Mauryan Empire began and how it was run.
teach.praise: Chandragupta and Chāṇakya, with the Arthashāstra as a guidebook. What a team!
teach.nudge: Great start! Who guided Chandragupta, and what book is linked with him?

revise.summary: Around 321 BCE, Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chāṇakya (Kauṭilya), overthrew the Nandas and founded the Mauryan Empire with its capital at Pāṭaliputra. The Arthashāstra explains statecraft, and Megasthenes described the court in Indica.
focus: Know who founded the Mauryan Empire and when
Know what the Arthashāstra is about and its seven limbs
Know the order Chandragupta, Bindusāra, Ashoka
remember: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire around 321 BCE
Chāṇakya = Kauṭilya; Arthashāstra = book on statecraft
Saptāṅga: king, ministers, territory with people, fort, treasury, army, allies
Megasthenes: Greek ambassador from Seleucus; wrote Indica
traps: Ashoka was the grandson, not the founder
Megasthenes was Greek, not a Chinese traveller
Saptāṅga has seven limbs, not five

learn.hook: After winning a terrible war, a mighty emperor decided to conquer hearts instead of lands.
points: Ashoka, grandson of Chandragupta, fought a war against Kalinga (in present-day Odisha). The great loss of life in this war filled him with sorrow.
After Kalinga, Ashoka gave up wars of conquest and followed dhamma: kindness, truthfulness, respect for elders and teachers, care for animals, and respect for all faiths.
He spread his message through edicts carved on rocks and pillars, mostly in Prakrit and in the Brāhmī script. In 1837 James Prinsep deciphered the Brāhmī script, so we can read them today.
Ashoka set up hospitals for people and animals, had wells dug and trees planted along roads, and sent messengers to other lands. His son Mahinda (Mahendra) took Buddhism to Sri Lanka.
The Lion Capital of his pillar at Sarnath is India's National Emblem, and the chakra on our national flag, with 24 spokes, comes from Ashoka's pillars.

example.q: Ashoka wrote his edicts on rocks and pillars along roads and near towns, in the people's language. Why?
steps: He wanted ordinary people, not just scholars, to learn about dhamma.
Rocks and pillars last a very long time and are seen by travellers.
Using Prakrit, a language people spoke, made the message easy to understand.
example.answer: So that many people could read or hear his message and it would last for a long time.

learn.reallife: Indian rupee notes and coins carry the Lion Capital from Sarnath, and the Ashoka Chakra sits at the centre of the Indian flag.

games.title: Ashoka's story
items: Edicts are carved on rocks and pillars

games.title: True or false: Ashoka
items: The Kalinga war took place in present-day Odisha.
Ancient Kalinga covered much of today's Odisha.
Most of Ashoka's edicts were written in the Brāhmī script.
Most were in Brāhmī; some in the north-west used other scripts.
Ashoka's dhamma asked people to respect all faiths.
Respect for other sects was a key part of his message.
The chakra on India's flag has 12 spokes.
India's National Emblem comes from Ashoka's Lion Capital at Sarnath.
It was adopted as the National Emblem in 1950.
Ashoka's edicts were first read again in the 20th century.
James Prinsep deciphered Brāhmī in 1837, in the 19th century.

quiz.q: Which war changed Ashoka's heart?
quiz.explain: The suffering caused by the Kalinga war made Ashoka give up conquest by war.
steps: Ashoka fought a war against Kalinga.
The great loss of life filled him with sorrow, and he gave up wars of conquest.
So the Kalinga war changed his heart.
Answer: The Kalinga war
quiz.mistake: Mixes up battles from different periods

quiz.q: Ancient Kalinga lay mostly in present-day:
quiz.explain: Kalinga covered much of today's Odisha on the east coast.
steps: Kalinga was on the east coast.
It covered much of present-day Odisha.
So the answer is Odisha.
Answer: Odisha
quiz.mistake: Does not place Kalinga on the map

quiz.q: Which script were most of Ashoka's edicts written in?
quiz.explain: Most edicts use Brāhmī, an ancient script from which many Indian scripts later developed.
steps: Ashoka's edicts were mostly in Prakrit.
They were written mostly in the Brāhmī script.
Devanagari and Roman are not the script of the edicts.
Answer: Brāhmī
quiz.mistake: Assumes they were written in a modern script

quiz.q: Who deciphered the Brāhmī script in 1837?
quiz.explain: James Prinsep, working in Kolkata, cracked the script in 1837.
steps: Brāhmī could not be read for a long time.
In 1837 James Prinsep deciphered it.
So the answer is James Prinsep.
Answer: James Prinsep
quiz.mistake: Picks another famous name linked with Indian history

quiz.q: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra on the national flag have?
quiz.explain: The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes.
steps: The chakra on India's flag comes from Ashoka's pillars.
It has 24 spokes.
So the answer is 24.
Answer: 24
quiz.mistake: Remembers the wheel but not its spokes

quiz.q: Which of these was part of Ashoka's dhamma?
options: Kindness to animals and respect for all faiths
quiz.explain: Dhamma stressed kindness, truth, respect for elders and tolerance.
steps: Ashoka's dhamma meant kindness, truth, respect for elders, care for animals and respect for all faiths.
He gave up war and did not force one religion.
So kindness to animals and respect for all faiths.
Answer: Kindness to animals and respect for all faiths
quiz.mistake: Thinks dhamma meant forcing one belief

quiz.q: India's National Emblem is taken from Ashoka's pillar at:
quiz.explain: The Lion Capital found at Sarnath near Varanasi was adopted as the emblem.
steps: India's National Emblem is the Lion Capital.
It was found on Ashoka's pillar at Sarnath, near Varanasi.
So the pillar is at Sarnath.
Answer: Sarnath
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Sarnath with other Buddhist sites

quiz.q: Which of Ashoka's children is linked with taking Buddhism to Sri Lanka?
quiz.explain: Ashoka's son Mahinda went to Sri Lanka with the Buddha's teachings.
steps: Ashoka's son was Mahinda (Mahendra).
Mahinda took Buddhism to Sri Lanka.
Bindusāra was his father and Chandragupta his grandfather.
Answer: Mahinda (Mahendra)
quiz.mistake: Confuses Ashoka's father or grandfather with his son

teach.ask: Gappu heard that Ashoka changed after a war. Tell him what happened and what Ashoka did next.
teach.praise: From war to kindness! And his lions and wheel are still on our money and flag.
teach.nudge: You told me about the war. What did Ashoka do afterwards to spread his message?

revise.summary: After the Kalinga war in present-day Odisha, Ashoka gave up conquest and followed dhamma: kindness, truth, respect for elders and all faiths, and care for animals. He spread it through edicts in Prakrit and Brāhmī, deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.
focus: Explain how the Kalinga war changed Ashoka
Know about his edicts, their language and script
Know Ashoka's legacy: Sarnath Lion Capital, Ashoka Chakra, Mahinda
remember: Kalinga war (Odisha) → Ashoka gave up wars of conquest
Edicts on rocks and pillars, mostly in Prakrit and Brāhmī; Prinsep deciphered Brāhmī in 1837
Sarnath Lion Capital = National Emblem; Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes
His son Mahinda (Mahendra) took Buddhism to Sri Lanka

The edicts are not in Devanagari
Mahinda was Ashoka's son, not his father
